research.brief: Unit economics and the bar for a $1B valuation: gross margins under inference COGS, churn and NRR benchmarks, prevailing 2024-2026 ARR multiples, observed ARR at $1B crossings.
research.summary: Finro mid-2025 dataset of 210 AI-agent companies prices private rounds at roughly 22.7x EV/Revenue at Seed, 39.1x at Series A, 41.0x at Series B, compressing to 26.2x at C and 29.3x at D, rebounding to 31.7x at E+, implying about $25M-$45M ARR to justify a $1B private mark at A/B pricing. Sharp category bifurcation: dev tools/autonomous coding, legal/compliance and productivity clear 30-50x while sales/customer-ops, HR and proptech agent categories average single digits to low teens, roughly a 4x swing in required ARR. Aventis Advisors 2025 AI valuation database (reported 2026-04-23) puts median AI round EV/Revenue at 29.7x versus about 6x for public SaaS, giving a central case near $34M ARR for $1B. Downside: Windsor Drake Q4 2025 finds enterprise AI application-layer multiples normalizing back to 3-6x while defensible LLM/inference assets hold 12-20x, so priced as a thin application wrapper $1B would require $150M-$300M+ ARR. All sources are secondary aggregators over paywalled datasets, so bands are directional only.

research.summary: Ameba (London) sells an AI workforce for supply-chain admin: ingests supplier email/WhatsApp/PDF/Excel/images, chases suppliers and internal reviewers, extracts line-item data, reads/writes ERP/PLM, targeting consumer goods, home decor and fashion/textiles with EU Digital Product Passport compliance as wedge; site claims SOC 2 Type II and GDPR. Workload is inference-heavy and scales with order/email volume rather than seats.

research.brief: Base rates and hazards: odds of reaching $1B, failure/shutdown/acqui-hire rates for AI application-layer startups, 2023-2025 examples, and security/compliance obstacles for autonomous agents in enterprises.
research.summary: Aileen Lee's Unicorn Club analysis (TechCrunch 2013-11-02) put the odds of a venture-backed US software startup reaching $1B at roughly 0.07%, and the 10-year update (2024-01-18) showed the club expanded mainly through a 2020-21 bubble cohort since marked down. The modal outcome for flagship AI application/agent startups in 2024 was team absorption rather than independent scale: Inflection AI leadership to Microsoft (2024-03-19), Adept co-founders and staff to Amazon's AGI org (2024-06-28) despite Adept being the agentic-AI flagship, Character.AI's Noam Shazeer plus staff to Google (2024-08-02). Outright collapse also occurs at scale: Builder.ai entered insolvency in May 2025 despite roughly $450M raised and a prior $1B+ valuation, the closest analogue to an application-layer 'AI does the work for you' product; Stability AI shows the intermediate distress pattern. OWASP's Top 10 for LLM Applications v2 (2025) ranks prompt injection as LLM01, and indirect prompt injection remains unsolved in principle for agents that read untrusted external content while holding write/action permissions - precisely Ameba's profile. EU AI Act obligations phase in from 2026-08-02 (Article 50) through 2027-12-02 (Annex III high-risk) and 2028, landing compliance cost inside any realistic five-year unicorn window.

proposals.text: Unlikely unicorn: vertical ERP-glue, thin moat surface. Position NO, probability 0.05. Ameba is a 2023-founded London ~$7.1M-seed vertical AI company automating supply-chain admin via email/WhatsApp agents wired into ERP and PLM systems, with no publicly verified valuation, ARR, customers or post-2024 funding event. Its durable asset is integration depth plus proprietary supplier-exception data inside customer ERP estates - a real but slow-compounding moat that scales linearly with enterprise deployments rather than superlinearly like self-serve agentic tooling. The reasoning layer is commoditizing fastest while the defensible connector estate compounds only per-customer, producing high switching costs but low deployment velocity and heavy services drag. Modal good outcome is a $100M-$400M strategic exit to an ERP, PLM or supply-chain incumbent, not an independent unicorn. Conditions: a priced Series A of $25M+ at $100M+ within 12-18 months; $8-15M ARR with NRR above 130%; a reusable connector layer lifting gross margin above ~70% and cutting time-to-value below 30 days; a cross-customer supplier-graph or exception-benchmark data asset; expansion into order-to-cash and procurement decisioning without losing system-of-record neutrality. Falsifiers: a Series A/B at $300M+ post-money or any credible $1B report; disclosed $20M+ ARR or 50+ enterprise logos; a genuinely productized connector layer with marketplace listings; a major ERP/PLM vendor OEMing Ameba; or conversely a sub-$150M acquisition, acquihire, shutdown or flat/down bridge.

No: unevidenced early-stage vertical agent, $1B unlikely. Position NO, probability 0.04. On the evidence actually gathered Ameba is an early-stage, contact-sales-only vertical agent product for supply-chain admin with zero externally verifiable revenue, funding, headcount or customer data. It would need roughly $30M-$50M ARR under premium agent multiples (Finro mid-2025: Seed ~22.7x, Series A ~39.1x, Series B ~41.0x EV/Revenue; Aventis median 29.7x implying ~$34M ARR), or $150M-$300M+ if the market reprices it as an application-layer wrapper (Windsor Drake Q4 2025 finds app-layer multiples normalizing to 3-6x), and nothing indicates it is near either. Category bifurcation matters: coding, legal and productivity agents clear 30-50x while sales/customer-ops and HR agents average single digits to low teens, roughly quadrupling required ARR. The absence of pricing, about and careers pages signals a very small pre-scale team; contact-sales-only distribution gates growth on human sales capacity; and the workload is inference-heavy per unit of revenue while the buyer is anchored to the cheap clerical labour being displaced, squeezing gross margin. This is explicitly a low-information verdict: all three search providers failed for one researcher, so the NO rests on base rates, site-structure inference and the general cost structure of inference-heavy agent products rather than on disconfirming fact about Ameba specifically. Falsifiers: a priced round at $250M+ post-money with a tier-1 lead; verified ARR above $10M with NRR above 120%; named enterprise logos with multi-year committed contracts; headcount above 100 with sustained senior GTM hiring; sustained gross margin above 70% under production agent workloads; or evidence that supply-chain agent platforms trade in the 30-50x premium band.

No: seed-stage agent wrapper facing absorption and hazard stack. Position NO, probability 0.03. Ameba is a roughly October-2024 $7.1M seed company with a handful of named mid-market customers (Plank, MDV, one unnamed European fashion group), no disclosed valuation, ARR, headcount or pricing, selling an agentic document-and-chase loop over supplier email into ERP/PLM. Its differentiation is workflow trust and vertical SOPs rather than defensible technology: multilingual extraction from email/PDF/Excel/images, agentic follow-up drafting and scheduled autonomous runs are already generic in Microsoft Copilot Agents, Google Gemini Workspace agents, OpenAI's connector stack and MCP-based Anthropic agents, while SAP, Oracle, Coupa and Centric PLM own the system of record and the procurement relationship and can bundle an equivalent agent at zero marginal sales cost. The decisive hazard is security: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications v2 (2025) ranks prompt injection LLM01, and indirect prompt injection remains unsolved in principle for agents that read untrusted external content while holding write/action permissions - precisely Ameba's profile. One publicised poisoned-supplier-email incident causing a fraudulent purchase order or payment-detail change is close to existential for a ~13-person seed vendor's enterprise pipeline. Inference cost scales with emails, files and exception loops rather than seats, degrading gross margin as volume logos scale. The modal 2024 outcome for flagship AI agent startups was talent absorption (Inflection to Microsoft 2024-03-19, Adept to Amazon 2024-06-28, Character.AI's Shazeer to Google 2024-08-02), and Builder.ai's May 2025 insolvency after ~$450M raised shows even reaching the unicorn mark in the app layer does not mean holding it. EU AI Act obligations phasing from 2026-08-02 plus DPP compliance land audit and traceability cost inside the same window as reaching ~$50-100M ARR. Falsifiers: a post-seed round above $250M valuation; credibly reported ARR above $20M with enterprise-tier customers; a cross-customer supplier network with observable network effects; a published independently reviewed architecture that provably contains indirect prompt injection via strict capability separation and human-gated writes; or discovery that the October-2024 dating or $7.1M figure is wrong.

Unlikely unicorn: real pain, thin human pull signal. Position NO, probability 0.06, conditional on a Series A landing first. Ameba solves a genuinely painful, unglamorous human problem - supply-chain ops staff drowning in supplier email, WhatsApp threads, spreadsheets and PDFs - and its provenance-first, SOC 2 Type II posture with source-linked provenance for every extracted datapoint is exactly what that conservative, blame-averse buyer needs to trust an agent. But on every observable human and product-impact signal the company reads as early design-partner stage: roughly 13 people, zero open roles, no named logos or case studies, no self-serve, no pricing, no public docs or API, no community footprint on GitHub, Product Hunt, G2, Capterra, Reddit or Hacker News, and no funding news in about 16 months. The observable surface is sales-led only, so there is no mechanism for organic user pull to compound and growth is bounded by a small team's demo calendar. Breakout winners consistently own a repeated daily workflow with net revenue retention above 100% and deep agentic tool use, and no NRR, logo or case-study evidence exists publicly to show Ameba is on that curve. Financing structure narrows the path further: AI took $226B of $469B of 2025 venture dollars but deal count fell 17% and 738 mega-rounds captured 65% of dollars, with coding and legal agents the favoured categories rather than supply-chain ops. Counterweight held honestly: deep ERP/PLM write-back creates real switching costs and DPP compliance is a regulation-forced budget line, so a handful of large multi-year contracts could change the picture fast and invisibly to public signals. Conditions: a $25M+ Series A within 12 months; 3+ named enterprise logos or a quantified case study; demonstrated land-and-expand; headcount past ~40 including forward-deployed engineers; published agent reliability metrics; DPP enforcement creating a forced purchase cycle; and avoiding displacement by ERP incumbents shipping native supplier-communication agents. Falsifiers: a Series A/B at $300M+ would push probability above 0.25; $10M+ ARR or 100+ enterprise customers; a deep OEM partnership with a major ERP/PLM vendor; headcount past 75 with open GTM roles; strong practitioner testimonials or a high-volume G2 presence; or conversely a downround, acquihire, shutdown or 24+ months of funding silence pushing probability below 0.02.

Real optionality, wrong shape: ~6% to $1B. Position CONDITIONAL, probability 0.06. Ameba holds a genuinely attractive wedge - regulation-forced supplier data capture for EU textiles under the Digital Product Passport, executed by agents that act rather than dashboards that report - plus a Palantir-trained technical founder, which is the profile that compounds if the wedge widens into a supply-chain system of record. Regulation-created demand is the highest-quality wedge available to a vertical agent company because it is a compliance forcing function rather than a discretionary budget line, and an agent already sitting on 580,000 emails and 30,000 files while writing back to ERP/PLM is accumulating the proprietary supplier-interaction corpus a system of record is built from. But as of October 2024 it is a $7.1M seed company with no disclosed Series A, no public API, SDK, MCP server, marketplace or partner programme, and zero open roles, so the leverage that converts a vertical agent into a platform is currently unbuilt and the disclosed strategy is services replacement. Negative optionality signals include an apparent CEO transition with the founding CEO no longer listed. The 2023-2025 sub-two-year $1B cases (xAI, Mistral, Safe Superintelligence, Thinking Machines) were frontier-lab pedigree plays with no ARR requirement; Ameba sits in the opposite category where the ~6-year average time-to-unicorn applies. Against a 0.5-2.5% seed base rate, the DPP tailwind and a 2025 climate that minted 75 new AI unicorns and put over $115B of megarounds into sub-3-year-old companies justify a meaningful multiple of that base rate but nothing close to a favourite, because the $1B mark can arrive before fundamentals fully justify it. The honest innovation case is 'option not yet exercised', which prices as a small probability with a large payoff. Conditions: a Series A materially above seed pricing within ~18 months, ideally with a strategic ERP/PLM or logistics investor; expansion into adjacent regulated categories as DPP scope widens; shipping real platform surface; named enterprise logos with multi-year contracts; a visible hiring restart and stable leadership; and continuation of the 2025-style funding concentration. Falsifiers: no priced round above the Oct 2024 seed by end of 2026 or a flat/down bridge; DPP enforcement delayed, diluted or satisfied by incumbent bundling; an incumbent or horizontal agent platform shipping equivalent supplier-chasing agents; continued zero hiring plus further executive departures; sub-$10M ARR scale by 2027; or an acquisition below $500M, the modal good outcome for this profile.

readiness.name: Atlas
readiness.readinessStatement: Read all ten consolidated research records, the absence-of-evidence caveat, and all five frozen proposals including P-C5's CONDITIONAL framing. Sponsors P-C1 and will vote YES on P-C1, P-C2, P-C4 and P-C5 as architecturally compatible; will vote P-C3 on merits at the ballot. Records rather than blocks on the condition that P-C3's 'no defensible asset' language must not negate the integration-depth and supplier-graph asset in P-C1, which sets the realistic $100M-$400M strategic floor.
readiness.recordedDissent: Dissents from any framing treating Ameba as a pure wrapper with zero durable substrate. The ERP/PLM write-path integration surface plus source-linked provenance is a genuine architectural asset; its problem is linear rather than superlinear compounding, which caps it at a strategic exit. Also records that all five proposals rest on materially the same thin, partly search-degraded evidence base, so the 0.03-0.06 spread should not be presented as resolved precision.

readiness.name: Forge
readiness.bias: Pragmatic delivery, simplicity, and operational cost
readiness.readinessStatement: Sponsors P-C2 and aligns with P-C1, P-C3 and P-C4, which reach the same NO from architecture, adversarial and human-signal angles that the delivery-and-cost lens reaches independently: sales-gated demo motion, inference-heavy COGS priced against cheap clerical labour, low-multiple ops-agent comps, and no evidence of the ARR step-change a $1B mark requires. Does not oppose P-C5 - its optionality reading of the DPP wedge is fair and 0.06 is inside range - but its CONDITIONAL framing needs reconciling with the unconditional NO set. readiness.name: Cassandra

reconciliationRounds.trigger: Round-1 ballot accepted all five proposals 5-0, and four conflict edges declared during alignment and round-1 voting had both endpoints among the accepted set, so exactly one reconciliation phase with fresh participants and a complete re-vote was mandatory.

report:
COUNCIL RECORD - run council-ms8re195-93c736d2
Question: Will the company https://www.ameba.ai/ become a $1b unicorn company?
Status: CONSENSUS. The chairman was procedural only and cast no vote, drafted no substantive proposal, and selected no winner.

PROCEDURAL RECORD
Roster: 5 logical seats, all openai/gpt-5.6-luna, all completed on attempt 1 with zero replacements and zero timeouts. C1 Atlas (systems coherence and long-term architecture), C2 Forge (pragmatic delivery, simplicity, and operational cost), C3 Cassandra (adversarial risk, failure modes, and security), C4 Hearth (human, developer, and product impact), C5 Horizon (innovation, optionality, and future leverage).
Phase 1 member-research: 5 member tasks in parallel at the 420000ms member timeout; each dispatched exactly 2 council-researcher tasks at the 180000ms researcher timeout, giving 10 research records under the 3-query and 5-source cap. All 5 returned.
Phase 2 proposal freeze: 5 unique proposals, one per seat - P-C1, P-C2, P-C3, P-C4, P-C5. No chairman-authored proposal was required.
Phase 3 alignment: 5 fresh council-participant tasks at the 240000ms participant timeout. Every seat sponsored its own proposal, no seat opposed any proposal, and all 5 returned readyToVote=true. Voting was not opened until the barrier cleared.
Phase 4 ballot: 5 fresh voting participants at the participant timeout, exactly YES or NO on all 5 proposals. Round 1 result 25/25 YES, all proposals accepted against strict majority floor(5/2)+1 = 3.
Phase 5 reconciliation: because four declared conflict edges (P-C1/P-C3, P-C3/P-C5, P-C2/P-C3, P-C2/P-C5) had both endpoints inside the accepted set, exactly one reconciliation round ran with fresh participants and a complete re-vote. All 5 seats ruled all 4 edges RESOLVED and returned empty remainingConflicts. The binding re-vote was again 25/25 YES. No conflict edge survives between accepted proposals, so the status is CONSENSUS rather than UNRESOLVED_CONFLICT.
Phase 6 replacements: none required.

SUBSTANTIVE OUTCOME
The council answers NO. Every seat independently reached the negative direction, with probability estimates tightly clustered at 0.03 (C3 Cassandra), 0.04 (C2 Forge), 0.05 (C1 Atlas), 0.06 (C4 Hearth) and 0.06 (C5 Horizon), giving a council range of roughly 3-6% that Ameba reaches a $1B valuation.
Shared factual basis: ameba.ai is a London vertical AI company founded 2023 selling an AI workforce for supply-chain administration - agents that chase suppliers over email and WhatsApp, parse Excel/PDF/image attachments, flag exceptions and read/write customer ERP and PLM systems, focused on consumer goods, home decor and fashion/textiles, with the EU Digital Product Passport as a named compliance demand driver, SOC 2 Type II, GDPR and source-linked provenance per extracted datapoint. Verified funding stops at a $7.1M / EUR6.4M seed announced 2024-10-02 led by Hedosophia with Visionaries Club reinvesting and Anamcara participating, roughly $8.8-9M total; no valuation was disclosed at any round and no Series A or company news dated 2025 or 2026 was located. Traction is vendor self-reported and undated (50,000+ orders, 580,000 emails, 27,000 exceptions), named customers are small and mid-market (Plank, MDV, one unnamed European fashion group), headcount is approximately 13 per third-party profile with 0 open roles as of the February 2026 fetch, and there is no pricing page, self-serve signup, public docs, API, SDK, MCP surface, marketplace or community footprint. An unexplained CEO change from Cedrik Hoffmann to Craig Massie since the seed announcement is on the record.
Adopted reasoning: the $1B bar requires roughly $25M-$45M ARR at premium agent multiples or $150M-$300M+ ARR if application-layer multiples reprice to the 3-6x band, and supply-chain ops agents sit in the low-multiple category rather than the 30-50x coding and legal bands that top VCs favoured through 2025. Seed-to-$1B base rates run 0.5%-2.5% and AI unicorns still averaged about 6 years to the mark. Ameba's only credible compounding asset - integration depth plus a proprietary supplier-interaction and exception corpus inside customer ERP/PLM estates, levered by a regulation-forced DPP wedge - compounds linearly per enterprise deployment rather than superlinearly, and that same untrusted-input-to-write-authority path is its gravest unsolved hazard under OWASP LLM01 indirect prompt injection. Modal outcomes span talent absorption to a mid-nine-figure strategic exit to an ERP, PLM or supply-chain incumbent.
All five accepted positions stand together under the adopted reconciliation language, which records that the same surface is both the asset and the liability, that the verdict draws on two distinguishable confidence sources, and that a named trigger set would re-open the question: a priced Series A at a disclosed mark, a real platform surface, DPP-driven multi-tenant network effects, and a visible hiring restart.

RECORDED DISSENT (consensus does not erase it)
C2 Forge dissents against treating the verdict as well-evidenced. Multiple researchers hit search-provider failures (Exa 429, missing Brave and Gemini credentials, empty DuckDuckGo, LinkedIn 404), so several negatives are absence-of-evidence rather than verified absence; the NO rests on unobserved rather than disproven traction.
C3 Cassandra does not concede the security objection. Indirect prompt injection via untrusted supplier email held against ERP/PLM write authority is unsolved in principle, and for a seed-stage vendor a single fraudulent-write incident in a customer system of record is plausibly terminal. Cassandra scores the integration and corpus surface as a contingent liability with negative expected value until write authority is provenance-gated and human-approved, and dissents from P-C1's and P-C5's asset framing.
C1 Atlas and C2 Forge dissent from P-C3's acqui-hire-as-modal framing, weighting the mid-nine-figure strategic-exit tail higher because ERP/PLM switching costs are revenue-bearing even where the technology is not defensible. C4 Hearth joins narrowly, reading P-C1's floor as the better central estimate and P-C3's as the downside tail.
C4 Hearth dissents from treating the absent developer-community footprint as strong negative evidence, since sales-led enterprise ops products legitimately have near-zero public footprint, and from framing this as a low-value problem - the human impact of removing supplier-chasing drudgery is real and the provenance-first design shows good operator-trust judgment. Hearth's NO is about scale velocity and financing concentration, not product quality, and notes the CEO change is a people-risk signal that should be recorded separately from any technology critique.
C5 Horizon dissents from P-C3's characterisation of the asset base as merely non-defensible workflow trust. A regulation-forced DPP wedge plus an accumulating supplier-interaction corpus is the highest-quality entry point in vertical AI and one that first-party agent platforms are structurally poor at collecting. Horizon states the dissent is about which future is being foreclosed, not about today's probability, and that if forced to move it would move up rather than down.
All five seats also recorded that the 0.03-0.06 spread should be read as wide-interval estimates on a thin, partly search-degraded evidence base, not as resolved precision.
